content:
Bloomberg reported today that Apple is about to launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" hardware leasing programme. The programme will let users get their hands on brand-new Apple products via a monthly subscription, though there are reports that the plan comes with several restrictions, let's hope they don't end up being true.

"Apple Upgrade" will make higher-priced products more accessible, but the programme reportedly won't include entry-level models

Affected by the current AI-driven memory chip shortage, most Apple products have recently seen price hikes.

This autumn, this upward pricing trend will further intensify, with newly launched iPhone and Apple Watch models expected to see price hikes as well. Higher-end iPhone Ultra and MacBook Ultra products will also make their debut.

According to Mark Gurman, Apple's response is to launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" hardware monthly subscription option.

Gurman said the option will launch next week simultaneously on Apple's online store and physical stores, applicable to purchases of designated products.

Before the final details are confirmed, I think this approach to making Apple products more affordable is a good direction.

Apple Upgrade will be entirely voluntary, so any user who wants to purchase products directly can still do so as usual. But given the recent wave of price hikes, adding more options seems to be a matter of course.

My only concern is the scope of eligible hardware. Gurman pointed out that some devices will not be included in Apple Upgrade, including the "Apple Watch SE, entry-level iPad, iPhone 16, and MacBook Neo".

It would be a shame if Apple doesn't allow users to choose its cheapest products through the leasing programme.

Imagine this: you've always found Apple products beyond your budget, but with this new programme, you can own a MacBook Neo for just US$20 a month. In this scenario, Apple Upgrade is expected to bring a large number of new users into the Apple ecosystem.

I understand Apple's thinking in wanting to encourage users to buy higher-priced products. But restricting Apple Upgrade to specific hardware seems to make the programme unnecessarily complicated and weakens its impact.

What do you think of the Apple Upgrade programme? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
